originalTitle: IRB Infrastructure Q1 profit zooms 51% YoY to Rs 306 crore
simplifiedContent: IRB Infrastructure, a company, made a profit of Rs 306 crore in the first quarter of the year, which is 51% more than what they made last year. This is a big increase and it's mainly because they had strong revenue, or income, during this time. The company's total income also went up a little bit compared to last year. This news matters because it shows that the company is doing well financially, which can be good for people who have invested in it. The company also announced that it will give some of its profit back to its investors as a dividend, which is a way for companies to share their profit with the people who own their shares.

originalTitle: Market wrap: M&M, Coal India, Adani Ports among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market had a good day on Thursday, with the main indexes (Sensex and Nifty) going up in value. The Sensex rose by 274 points and the Nifty ended above 24,300. This happened after the US central bank (US Fed) decided not to change interest rates. Some companies, like M&M, Coal India, and Maruti Suzuki, did well and their stock prices went up, while others, like Adani Ports, HDFC Life, and Shriram Finance, did poorly and their prices went down. This means that investors who own stocks in the winning companies might be happy, while those who own stocks in the losing companies might not be as happy.

originalTitle: AI Big Short? Why rising credit default swaps are spooking investors and how is it similar to 2008 housing crisis
simplifiedContent: Here's what's happening: some big technology companies are seeing a rise in "credit default swaps", which is a kind of insurance that protects investors if those companies can't pay their debts. This is making investors nervous and worried that the market might be in for a big correction, or drop. Some are comparing this to what happened in 2008 with the housing crisis, when one investor correctly bet against the market. This matters because it could mean that the market is getting too hot and might be due for a downturn, which could affect investors' money. The rise in spending on artificial intelligence and high company values are adding to these concerns.

originalTitle: Vedanta Q1 results: Profit rises 72% YoY to  ₹5,473 crore; names new CEO, announces real estate business demerger
simplifiedContent: Vedanta, a company, recently shared its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company's profit increased by 72% compared to the same time last year, reaching ₹5,473 crore. This is a significant improvement, indicating that the company is performing well. The company's total revenue from its operations also increased by 53.6% to ₹24,205 crore, which is a good sign for the company's growth. This news matters because it shows that Vedanta is doing well financially, which can affect the company's stock price and be important for investors to know.

originalTitle: Swiggy Q1 results: Net loss narrows to  ₹791 crore; revenue jumps 37% YoY
simplifiedContent: Swiggy, a food delivery company, recently shared its financial results for the first quarter of the fiscal year 2027. The company's net loss, which is the amount of money it lost, decreased to ₹791 crore from ₹1,197 crore in the same quarter last year. This is a positive sign, as it means the company is losing less money than before. Swiggy's revenue, which is the amount of money it earned, increased by 37% to ₹6,812 crore, mostly due to growth in its quick commerce services. This increase in revenue and decrease in loss suggests that the company is performing better than it was a year ago.

originalTitle: Bajaj Finance Q1 Results: Net profit jumps 27% to  ₹5,986 crore; NII up 23%
simplifiedContent: Bajaj Finance, a financial company, just reported its quarterly earnings and they're very good. The company made a net profit of ₹5,986 crore, which is 27% more than it made during the same time last year. This beats what most people were expecting, which is a positive sign. The company also made more money from interest on loans, with a 23% increase, and its total assets grew by 23% to ₹4,00,389 crore. This matters because it shows the company is performing well, which can affect its stock price and be important for investors to know.
